question.prompt:
Haruki has a piece of wire that is \(24\) centimeters long. He wants to bend it to form each of the following shapes, one at a time.

A regular hexagon with side length \(5\) cm.

A square of area \(36\) cm².

A right triangle whose legs are \(6\) and \(8\) cm long.

Which of the shapes can Haruki make?

solutions.explanation:
Bending the wire changes its shape but preserves its length, so compare each shape’s perimeter with \(24\) cm.

A regular hexagon has six equal sides. Its perimeter is \(6\times5=30\) cm, so the wire is too short.

The square has side length \(6\) cm because \(6\times6=36\). Its perimeter is \(4\times6=24\) cm, so Haruki can make it.

For the right triangle, the Pythagorean theorem gives the hypotenuse length as
\[
\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10\text{ cm}.
\]
We take the positive square root because this is a length. The triangle’s perimeter is \(6+8+10=24\) cm, so Haruki can make it too.

Therefore, he can make the square and triangle only, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the required perimeters
